questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The reputation of the University on Europes best universities

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy. The general information was given fairly in advance but more specific information on courses came a little late.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Purely information online via mail correspondance with the mobility adminstrator.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Very difficult. Leuven is a place with limited housing for students so it would be a very good idea to find housing way ahead of your semesterstart as the accomodations run out quickly and it gives unnessecary stress on your semesterstart.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: To not get lonely it is smart to find work groups or social groups early as this is not build upon when the semester starts. Living off campus is nice but can be lonesome.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You get an email with many instructions and many informations to fill in. It can be triggy to figure out everything you need to do and then later comes the course selection process which can also be a little stressful.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Online forum to ask any kinds of questions to the student service with quick reply's.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Not that succesful as I had to change before starting because of courses overlapping. In my experience it would have been better to inform students on when the course is scheduled in a week to earlier choose the right courses.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Figure out courses and take as much time as needed to pick them, it is essential that you choose the correct courses so that you dont end up having overlapping courses or courses which are too difficult for you.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level is quite high, Belgium students have lots of rote learning which I was not particullary experienced in, and it can give quite the workload.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Style of teaching were quite the same but there were no practise lessons where you could hone your skills from the lectures but all in all teaching is very similar.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Supply Chain Management 
Capital Investment Policy 
Consumer Behaviour 
Incentives and Behaviour 
Macro Finance

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Consumer Behaviour was a great course with a really good teacher and structure. No ordinary exam but a questionair each week with questions from the week which was really nice. Incentives and Behaviour was a MA course and great structure and great teacher.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Citytax is important to get registrered at city hall so you dont get to pay that much in citytax.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Transportation was a little expensive but not that much.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Many different sports and cultural activities such as visits in other cities of Belgium, parties, sportscard to use the fascilities etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Parties at the ekonomika student association. They make great activities for the international students aswel.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Visit other cities in Belgium. Leuven is quite small and can be boring at times but there are many nice cities in Belgium. Gent, Genk, Bruxelles and Antwerpen.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite easy, there are not that many cultural differences between Belgium and Denmark.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go to activities orchestrated by the associations!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not any in particular

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Party culture mostly.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Very hard university with hard courses and prepare for a big workload 
Very nice student organisations and plenty of activities 
Be keen on choosing the right courses! It is important.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be present at facebook very early to find student accomodation.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Experiencing another university and its study approach. Also makes me appreciate what we have at UCPH.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Courses and staying on top of the workload plus exams. Exams were very hard.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
